clue.text: To make it as an officer, try to look sexy holding bottom?

definitions.text: To make it as an officer

indicators.note: one thing holding another grips it inside, so the second word sits within the first

parts.note: to pout is to push the lips out in a sultry way
ass is slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A would-be officer cadet tries flirting their way through the passing-out parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Military cadets pass out when they complete training and are commissioned; the comma-free run of words hides where the definition ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing out is the British term for graduating from a military academy and being commissioned.

clue.text: Available and quite amenable to gropes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: there for anyone to take
second meaning, read literally: willing to be grabbed

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning takes the idiom at face value, as someone happy to be grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means obtainable by whoever reaches first, and its literal reading suits someone inviting grabs.

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Not a thing to be put up addict on trip

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up writes it from bottom to top

parts.note: a fan is a devotee or addict
to trip is to fall over

explanation.surface: Something you should never hoist an addict onto during a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: NAFF ALL is British slang for nothing at all; the surface trip suggests drugs, but here it is a stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff all is a British slang phrase meaning nothing whatsoever, a polite variant of a ruder expression.

clue.text: Casual habit? Dependency

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted pullover, informal clothing
second meaning: a Channel Island that is a British Crown Dependency

explanation.walkthrough: Habit means clothing here, not an addiction; Jersey is a self-governing island off France under the British Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a casual knitted top, and Jersey is one of the British Crown Dependencies.

clue.text: Not having sex muscles can — consequently lacks aspiration

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy h sound, so lacking it means losing that letter

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles
a tin is a can
hence means therefore

explanation.surface: A gym-toned celibate whose breathing gives out.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the aspirate h from HENCE leaves ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is refraining from something, especially sexual activity or alcohol.

clue.text: Boozer recruited by a political party (alien set of characters)

indicators.note: someone recruited by a group is taken into its ranks, so goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
Lab is short for the Labour Party
ET is the film alien
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A drunk is signed up by a party, along with an odd bunch of characters.
explanation.walkthrough: The boozer is taken in by the party itself, not by the whole string. The brackets make 'alien set of characters' look like an aside about the party.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabet is the full set of letters, or characters, used to write a language.

clue.text: Bill in middle of a 69, say? You could count on it

indicators.note: placing one thing in the middle of another sets it inside

parts.note: a number 69 is an example of a bus route
ac, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A sexual position comes with a bill attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The 69 is a bus number, not what the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads for counting, so literally something you count on.

clue.text: Business organisation supplying cocaine (undiscriminating, sex-wise)

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine
bi is short for bisexual

explanation.surface: A business lobby caught dealing coke to all comers.
explanation.walkthrough: The CBI is the Confederation of British Industry, a UK employers' lobby group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Confederation of British Industry is the main UK body representing employers and companies.

clue.text: Pay up? Beneath a front-bencher?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a high-backed wooden bench, so what someone on a bench sits on

explanation.walkthrough: A front-bencher sounds like a senior MP, but read literally it is anyone sitting on a bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to pay a debt, and a settle is an old wooden bench with a high back.

clue.text: Blanket coverage of 'New Conservative' Henry in the shit?

indicators.note: something in a substance is surrounded by it

parts.note: poo is excrement
N for new and C for Conservative
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Press reports on a new Tory MP called Henry who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Blanket coverage sounds like saturation news reporting, but a poncho is a blanket you wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a garment made from a blanket-like piece of cloth with a hole for the head.

clue.text: Eat and go pooh

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wolf down food
second meaning: to say pooh to something, to mock it

explanation.walkthrough: Pooh is the dismissive exclamation, not the bodily function the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is both to gobble food greedily and to jeer at something with contempt.

clue.text: Clare has inclination to put a candidate in the running

definitions.text: to put a candidate in the running

parts.note: Clare Short was a Labour cabinet minister
a list is a lean, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A politician named Clare is inclined to back a candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short was a British Labour MP and cabinet minister under Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: To shortlist someone is to include them on the final selection list of contenders.

clue.text: Only dug nuts like Dawkins?

indicators.note: something nuts is crazy, so these letters go haywire

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone who digs only nuts, the way Richard Dawkins might.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Dawkins is a famous British atheist, author of The God Delusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungodly means without religious belief, fitting a prominent atheist campaigner.

clue.text: One with habit of tossing turd over — I say! — penis, almost

indicators.note: tossing things throws them about into a new order
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
gad is a mild old oath, as in by gad
dick is slang for the penis

explanation.surface: A crude tale of someone flinging excrement and exposing themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: DICK loses its last letter, then TURD, GAD and DIC are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit here is an addiction, so one with a habit is a dependent drug user.

clue.text: Restraint is excellent when restraining naff Tory reactionary leaders

indicators.note: restraining something holds it in, so it sits inside

parts.note: cool means great

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A political commentator praises reining in naff reactionary Tory leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or uncool.
explanation.definitionFit: Control and restraint are synonyms for keeping something in check.

clue.text: Idle shit or bollocks behind which police hide

indicators.note: bollocks is British slang for a mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An outburst of abuse about lazy rubbish that the police cower from.
explanation.definitionFit: Riot police carry large transparent shields to protect themselves from thrown objects.

clue.text: see 18dn.
(& 17ac.) "Foul Females I Jiggered", Boris's literary tour de force?

indicators.note: something jiggered is broken or messed up, so the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
Boris Johnson, former UK Prime Minister, so the surname belonging to Boris

explanation.surface: A scurrilous title is offered as Boris Johnson's great book.
explanation.walkthrough: The real book is James Boswell's 1791 biography; the clue mischievously hands it to Boris, whose surname supplies the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Boswell's biography of the lexicographer is widely regarded as the greatest biography in English.

clue.text: OK for a consumer hack spewing bile

parts.note: ed, an editor, is a newspaper hack

indicators.note: spewing something sends it out in a disordered gush

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A splenetic journalist rants, though the product passes consumer standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible food is fit to eat, so safe for someone consuming it.

clue.text: Bear getting hots badly when hugging Bud

indicators.note: to hug something is to wrap around it
done badly, the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
Bud and Mac are both American ways to address a man

explanation.surface: A bear fancies its buddy and gives him a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal from the surface, but it is a verb meaning to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate it, a synonym for bear in the sense of endure.

clue.text: Wills' parent getting some stick, describing Kate's side?

parts.note: Prince William's mother was Diana, known as Di
a staff is a long stick

explanation.surface: Princess Diana takes flak for describing her daughter-in-law's family.
explanation.walkthrough: Wills is Prince William; Kate is his wife, so her side of the family is the female side.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side means the female line of a family, from the spinning tool associated with women.

clue.text: Parliament wants Ken's broadcast fixed

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so these letters are scattered too

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
set means fixed in place

explanation.surface: Parliament wants to rig a broadcast by a politician called Ken.
explanation.definitionFit: The Knesset is the national legislature of Israel.

clue.text: Familiar UK spy putting on Yoko's robe?

indicators.note: putting one thing on another places them together, one after the other

parts.note: Kim Philby, the Soviet double agent, known by his familiar name
Yoko Ono, John Lennon's widow

explanation.surface: A British spy wearing Yoko Ono's dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim Philby was a British intelligence officer who spied for the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a loose Japanese robe, apt for a Japanese-born artist.

clue.text: Business fat cats here beam at latitude?

parts.note: a board is a plank of timber, like a beam
latitude means scope or room to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Overpaid executives smile at the freedom they enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Beam looks like a verb for smiling, but it is a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A boardroom is where company directors, the highly paid fat cats, hold their meetings.

clue.text: see 3dn.
Rip nuts with S&M, which makes you really see the light

definitions.text: which makes you really see the light

indicators.note: something nuts is crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
the letters of S&M without the ampersand

explanation.surface: A painful sadomasochistic episode that brings an epiphany.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism splits white light into its colours, so it shows what light is made of.

clue.text: Bung, brute of a thing, Labour's no. 1 accepted

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so it sits inside

parts.note: a pug is a small snub-nosed dog, ironically a brute

indicators.note: number one of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A thuggish figure is given a bribe and Labour's top man goes along.
explanation.walkthrough: Bung reads as a bribe from the surface, but here it is a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug and a bung are both stoppers that seal a hole.

clue.text: Intertwine tops of erotic naked limbs, hotshot!

indicators.note: the tops of words are their initial letters

parts.note: the first letter of each word
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An instruction to a skilled lover to wrap bare limbs together.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlace is to wind or twist things together, a literary synonym of intertwine.

clue.text: When others are around trendy bar, there's no end of arses

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter is cut off

parts.note: in means fashionable
a pub is a bar
the verb that goes with arses in the phrase for toadying

explanation.surface: A trendy bar is full of idiots whenever there is company.
explanation.walkthrough: The last piece seems to lean on licking arses, as a creep does, with K dropped; the link is loose, typical of this setter's crude humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in public means doing it openly, where other people can see.
